name: Array Without Local Maximums
description: Ivan unexpectedly saw a present from one of his previous birthdays. It is array of $$$n$$$ numbers from $$$1$$$ to $$$200$$$. Array is old and some numbers are hard to read. Ivan remembers that for all elements at least one of its neighbours ls not less than it, more formally: $$$a_{1} \le a_{2}$$$, $$$a_{n} \le a_{n-1}$$$ and $$$a_{i} \le max(a_{i-1}, \,\, a_{i+1})$$$ for all $$$i$$$ from $$$2$$$ to $$$n-1$$$. Ivan does not remember the array and asks to find the number of ways to restore it. Restored elements also should be integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$200$$$. Since the number of ways can be big, print it modulo $$$998244353$$$.
input_specification: First line of input contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 10^{5}$$$) — size of the array. Second line of input contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_{i}$$$ — elements of array. Either $$$a_{i} = -1$$$ or $$$1 \le a_{i} \le 200$$$. $$$a_{i} = -1$$$ means that $$$i$$$-th element can't be read.
output_specification: Print number of ways to restore the array modulo $$$998244353$$$.
approach_summary: Formulate expectation as E[X] = ∑ P(e) * v(e). Formulate linear transition equations on states and solve via DAG DP or Gaussian elimination.
